name: BlockNovas

attribution.legal_posture: Trend Micro source-reported fictitious recruiting entity and campaign assessment; this record carries no registered-company determination, charge, adjudication, or civil identity.

caveats: BlockNovas is represented as a vendor-reported fictitious recruiting entity; registration and legal-person status remain unverified.
Job applicants targeted with malware are victims; victim profiles are outside the DPRK-worker records.
This record retains no domains, IP addresses, email values, social-account identifiers, victim data or malware implementation details.
The source-assessed relationship covers its named activity; Void Dokkaebi, BeaverTail, fake-interview, and fraudulent-employment scope requires separate source links.

statements: Trend Micro describes BlockNovas as a fictitious company with recruiting presences used to lure software professionals into non-existent positions.
Trend Micro links the interview flow to a camera-update pretext and BeaverTail-related malware.
The same report assesses a relationship between DPRK-aligned IT-worker activity and Void Dokkaebi-related campaigns through layered Russian anonymization infrastructure.

sources.support: Trend Micro describes BlockNovas as a fictitious company used to lure software professionals into fraudulent interviews. It reports recruitment presence on LinkedIn, Upwork, and Freelancer and an automated camera-update pretext that delivered BeaverTail-related malware. The report separately assesses that DPRK-aligned IT workers and Void Dokkaebi-related campaigns used layered Russian VPN, proxy, VPS, and RDP infrastructure for recruitment sites, communications, cryptocurrency services, and other activity. Evidence boundary: Vendor campaign assessment. BlockNovas is a source-reported fictitious recruiter, not a verified legal company or civil identity. Job applicants targeted with malware are victims and are not represented as fraudulent workers. Shared infrastructure or source-assessed relationship does not merge all fake-interview malware and remote-employment activity
